front.title: Non-Collapse Semantics for Authorization, Evidence, and Execution State

abstract.t:
Distributed authorization systems frequently combine observations, policy evaluations, evidence records, authorization decisions, and execution receipts. Treating these different objects as interchangeable can create fail-open behavior, stale-authority bugs, and false claims of completion.
This document defines non-collapse semantics: explicit typed transitions between observation, evidence, authorization, and execution state; fail-closed treatment of missing or indeterminate premises; and comparison rules for determining when heterogeneous representations agree on a declared invariant. The document is informational and defines no new wire protocol.
